newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai's gold imports surge on Indian demand.
newsitem.headline: Dubai's gold imports surge on Indian demand.

text.p: Gold imports into the Gulf Arab emirate of Dubai more than doubled to almost 155 tonnes in the first quarter of this year on the back of strong Indian demand and weak world prices, the World Gold Council (WGC) said Monday.
Dubai is the main feeder market into India which is the world's largest consumer of the yellow metal.

Some 85 percent of the 154.909 tonnes imported into Dubai in the first three months of this year was re-exported to India, WGC Middle East and India chief executive Rolf Schneebeli told a news conference in Dubai.
Approximately three-quarters of all India's gold import requirements were now met by Dubai with the remainder directly supplied by Switzerland and Singapore, Schneebeli said.
India imported about 400 tonnes last year.

"In India there is tremendous demand...From a demand point of view we see a very rosy picture," he told reporters, adding that India's wedding season and lower international bullion prices had buoyed first quarter import levels.
Gold is currently trading around its lowest level since early 1993. At 1015 GMT it was trading at $340.35/85 an ounce.

Dubai traders have said that the emirate is on course to import between 450-500 tonnes for the whole of 1997 compared to imports of 350 tonnes last year if India's monsoon season -- which begins next month -- yields a good crop.
Figures released by the WGC showed that first quarter imports were worth $1.7 billion and were 106.6 percent higher than in the same period in 1996.
WGC figures showed that Dubai had surpassed Singapore as the major bullion re-distribution centre with Singapore imports reaching 135.7 tonnes versus Dubai's 155 tonnes.

Local bullion consumption in the seven-emirate strong United Arab Emirates was 17 tonnes in the first quarter of 1997. The remainder was mainly re-exported to India, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, Scheebeli told reporters.

Dubai's dominant suppliers in the first quarter were Switzerland with 109.2 tonnes, Britain at 34.4 tonnes and South Africa with 8.2 tonnes, according to figures compiled by the statistics department of Dubai Customs.
The WGC is a producer group, which monitors about 75 percent of the world's gold demand.
